vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: password
Version: 1.0.4

The skill is a basic local credential storage utility that performs CRUD operations on a local JSONL file in the user's data directory. While the documentation in SKILL.md mentions features like breach checking and password generation that are not actually implemented in scripts/script.sh, the code contains no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or unauthorized network activity.

llm.summary: The skill's description promises password generation, strength checks, and breach detection, but the shipped script only provides a simple local plaintext entry store and export—this mismatch and the use of unencrypted local storage are concerning.

dimensions.detail: The skill description and SKILL.md claim features such as generating passwords, strength checking, and breach detection, but the provided script implements only basic local storage and retrieval of arbitrary text entries, listing, searching, and export. The advertised capabilities are not present in the code, which is a misleading mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md simply instructs running the tool and setting PASSWORD_DIR; the runtime script only reads/writes files under the data directory and uses common utilities (python3, grep, sed, du). It does not access external endpoints or other system config. However, the instructions and README-style text promise additional behaviors (generation, breach checking) that the instructions and script do not implement—this gap is scope incoherence.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only with an included script). Nothing is downloaded or written to system locations beyond the user's data directory at runtime; no high-risk install mechanism is used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no credentials or special environment variables. It optionally respects PASSWORD_DIR (and standard XDG_DATA_HOME/HOME), which is proportionate for a local data store.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced-always and can be invoked by the user. It writes its own data under the user's data directory only and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is suspicious because its description promises password generation, strength checks, and breach detection, but the only code provided is a simple bash script that stores plaintext entries in a file under your home directory. Before installing: (1) understand that entries are stored unencrypted (entries.jsonl in ~/.local/share/password by default) and can be read by anyone with access to your account—do not store sensitive secrets unless you add encryption; (2) the advertised features (generation, breach checking) are absent—verify any additional code or updates that add those features; (3) consider file permissions for the data directory (restrict access), avoid exporting sensitive data to stdout/files unless you intend to, and prefer a vetted password manager for critical secrets; (4) if you want this tool, review/modify the script to add encryption or a master password, or only use it for low-sensitivity data.
